$description: The one source of ELA's design system (ADR 0042). tokens.css, specimen-switch.css and index.html are derived from this file by scripts/generate_design_system.py. Direction, in the user's words: «stile Apple, futuristico stile JARVIS, azzurro e bianco per tutto, premium». The leaf envelope and the alias syntax come from the W3C Design Tokens format; the values do not, and this file does not claim to conform. A semantic colour may carry $alpha; the palette stays opaque.

azure.$description: The colour of ELA's identity, with white: the sphere, the light of everything ELA does, the primary action.

slate.$description: The grey-blue of the light theme: its borders and its shadows, never black.

orb.$description: The glass of the sphere, which the theme changes: dark glass with an edge of light here, pale glass in the light theme. What keeps its hue across the themes is the light inside (color.light).

line.$description: The one inner edge of the glass: darkest at the top right, almost nothing where the light falls.

sheen.$description: The broad, faint reflection of the room, at 10–14%.

hotspot.$description: The small, sharp reflection of the room.

mask.$description: Only its alpha counts: what a mask keeps. It fades the light inside into the glass, and the sheen before the rim.

light.$description: The light inside the sphere, by role: c is the light, c2 its paler heart, veil the light thinned out. The same hue in both themes; on the white room it is darker and more saturated, or it would vanish (tests/design/test_contrast.py).

tone.$description: Numbers and sizes that depend on the theme.

ambient.$description: How much of the halo around the sphere shows. A halo on white dirties it: half, in the light theme.

hotspot.$description: The half-width and half-height of the hot spot: 7% by 5% of the sphere.

orb.$description: Pale glass: white at 10–20%, a grey-blue edge, a lighter grey-blue shadow. A dark shell over white loses its transparency and turns the sphere into a grey marble.

line.$description: The one inner edge of the glass: darkest at the top right, almost nothing where the light falls.

sheen.$description: The broad, faint reflection of the room, at 10–14%.

hotspot.$description: The small, sharp reflection of the room. Fainter on the white room, where white on azure shows more.

mask.$description: Only its alpha counts: what a mask keeps. It fades the light inside into the glass, and the sheen before the rim.

light.$description: The light inside the sphere, by role: c is the light, c2 its paler heart, veil the light thinned out. The same hue in both themes; on the white room it is darker and more saturated, or it would vanish (tests/design/test_contrast.py).

tone.$description: Numbers and sizes that depend on the theme.

ambient.$description: Half the dark theme's: a halo on white dirties it.

hotspot.$description: Smaller on the white room: white on azure shows more there.

sans.$description: The system stack: San Francisco on Mac and iPhone, Segoe UI on Windows. The only lawful way to have San Francisco (ADR 0042).

eyebrow.$description: A small label above what it names: upper case, widely tracked.

key.$description: The key of a state, a risk or an attention level, rendered as text.

min.$description: The narrowest a cell of a fluid grid may be before the grid wraps.

wide.$description: How many columns a wide cell spans.

material.$description: Glass and the room. The blur and the saturation of what is behind a pane; the two cold lights of the room and the glow at its centre.

start.$description: Where the vignette begins, from the centre out.

phone.$description: The width of the iPhone composition: 390 px.

section.$description: What a section of the specimen is taken to be tall before it is rendered.

field.$description: The widest a field grows: beyond this a line of text is too long to read back.

cell.$description: The narrowest cell of the grid of states on the specimen page.

mark.$description: The circle of a step of the plan.

dot.$description: The luminous dot of a pill.

presence.$description: ELA's presence is a sphere of light held in glass, drawn in CSS and nothing else. From the back: a contact shadow that sets it on the plane, a soft halo, the far half of an orbit of particles and of a thin ring, the glass shell with one inner edge, a continuous volume of light at two depths turning in opposite senses over a bed of light, a white core that breathes and drifts, an occlusion away from the light, a band of light that sweeps the glass, a rim light at the bottom right, a Fresnel edge on the lower half, the reflection of the room — a broad faint sheen and a small sharp hot spot, both fixed, which is what makes the turning readable — and the near half of the orbits. The state is the light: its colour, its rhythm, its intensity.

rest.$description: The state the header of the specimen page shows.

ground.$description: The contact shadow: a dark, blurred ellipse just under the sphere.

blur.$description: As a share of the size, like every blur and offset of the sphere.

border.$description: The one inner edge, as an offset inner shadow: the offset points to the bottom left, so the edge is darkest at the top right and vanishes where the light falls, at the top left.

fade.$description: Where the light inside begins to fade into the glass: no edge where the plasma ends.

far.$description: The far light: larger, blurrier, slower, darker; it turns against the near light. Over a bed of light, so the volume has no gaps.

bed.$description: A very large, very faint light under the clouds: the volume never has a gap.

near.$description: The near light: smaller, sharper, faster.

drift.$description: How far the core wanders from the centre, as a share of the size.

kind.$description: What the core of the sphere is in a state: how lit, how large, and whether it moves.

start.$description: Where the shade away from the light begins, from the top right.

rim.$description: The second light: at the bottom right, coloured by the light of the state, soft.

fresnel.$description: A thin luminous edge on the lower half of the silhouette, strongest at the bottom, in the colour of the light. The upper half has the one inner edge of the glass.

sheen.$description: The broad, faint reflection of the room: an ellipse tangent to the curve of the glass at the top left, fading before the rim. Fixed.

hotspot.$description: The small, sharp reflection of the room, where the light falls: a defined edge, not a cut one. Fixed. Its size is a token of each theme (tone.hotspot).

orbit.$description: An orbit around the sphere: a circle tilted into an ellipse. Its far half is drawn behind the glass, its near half in front.

particles.$description: Round points on a tilted orbit. The orbit squashes whatever it carries, so each point is stretched back by 1 / cos(tilt) and turns against the orbit at its speed: on screen it stays a point.

ring.$description: A very thin equatorial ring, tilted, that passes behind the glass and in front of it.

sweep.$description: A faint band of light that crosses the glass now and then, like a reflection on something that turns.

state.$description: The states of ELA. The keys are the titles of section 6 of docs/spec/ELA_design.md, verbatim and in order: tests/design/test_lists.py reads them from the document. The key is also the label. A state is the light of the sphere: its colour (light), its rhythm (spin, and whether it turns at all), its intensity (glow), its core, and the colour of its key as text. Azure for everything ELA does; grey when it is still or gone; amber, orange and red only for the states that ask for the user or report a fault.

risk.$description: The keys are the values of ela.domain.RiskLevel, verbatim and in order: what the API already answers. One ramp for risk and for attention: grey, azure, amber, orange, red.

attention.$description: The keys are the levels of section 13 of docs/spec/ELA_design.md, verbatim and in order. ADR 0042 decides that these are the names the domain will inherit.

contrast.$description: Every pair of a foreground and the background it is drawn on. The threshold is not declared here: it derives from the group of fg. A colour with alpha is composed over surface.base before it is measured (tests/design/test_contrast.py).
